answer: Each agent identity must lock a fixed bond before claiming work, and a random audit can slash it when supposedly independent agents reuse proof or submit coordinated duplicates. The audit signal is public, while onyx and opal name separate audit queues so an attacker cannot predict which claims get checked. Spawning 1,000 Sybils therefore ties up 1,000 bonds and exposes each to forfeiture; cheap identities no longer mean cheap voting power.
